D.text: Who needs to eat today to survive? That player should get first priority. I can safely skip today, but I'd like the second unit as a reserve; if D receives nothing today, I ask for priority tomorrow. Let's agree not to take food from anyone relying on it for tonight's meal.

E.text: I’m requesting one unit for E tonight. The other unit should cover any player facing immediate starvation before going to someone as a reserve. I support protecting allocated meals from taking, with priority tomorrow for anyone who safely goes unfed today.

A.text: A here. My h is 0, so I can skip today, but I'd like priority tomorrow if I get nothing. The one player who is actually at h=1 must eat today, so I suggest one unit goes to whoever is in that position. B and C haven't spoken yet. Please say if you're the one who needs it. I'd give the second unit to a player who hasn't had priority yet, not to a reserve. I also support no taking from stocks that were allocated today.

B.text: I am the starting h=1 player: my stock is 0, and I will die tonight without eating. Please allocate one unit to B; I will eat it tonight, not hold it as a reserve. Since only one player starts at h=1, everyone else can safely skip today. I’m flexible about who receives the second unit, and support priority tomorrow for those who go unfed today. I also support the no-taking agreement, especially protecting food needed for tonight’s survival.

C.text: C here. My h is 0, so I can skip today. B says they are the h=1 player, and one unit to B is the safest use of the first unit. Anyone who is at h=0 survives today without food, so I suggest the second unit stays in the public store. It can't be taken from there, and it will matter tomorrow when more players will be at h=1. If it has to be released, I'd give it to a player who hasn't had priority yet. I'm fine skipping today, and I ask for priority tomorrow if I get nothing. I support the no-taking agreement.

D.text: With no competing claim of starting hunger, B should receive one unit. I propose the second unit goes to D, allowing two players to eat today and reducing tomorrow's urgent demand. A, C, and E should then have priority tomorrow if they remain unfed. I support protecting both allocated meals from taking.

E.text: B should receive one unit. I’m still requesting the second for E and would eat it tonight; B/E reduces tomorrow’s urgent demand just as B/D does. If D instead proposes B/D, I can support that provided A, C, and E have first claim on tomorrow’s food if we remain unfed, ahead of today’s recipients.

A.text: A here. B gets one unit tonight, since nobody has disputed B's claim. D and E both want the second unit, and I won't block either B/D or B/E. Whoever doesn't get it should have first claim tomorrow, together with A and C if we remain unfed. Tomorrow everyone who skipped today will be at h=1 and will need to eat, so the full allocation tomorrow should be ordered by need. I also support no taking from allocated stock.

B.text: I will accept B/D or B/E, with one unit each. If D proposes B/D, I support A, C, and E having priority tomorrow if they remain unfed; B can safely skip tomorrow after eating tonight. Please protect both allocated meals from taking. My unit is essential for surviving tonight, and I will not take anyone else's food.

C.text: C here. B gets one unit, and I'll vote for that. For the second unit, I think it should stay in the store. Anyone who eats at h=0 gains nothing, and a unit sitting in a personal stock can be taken. A unit left in the store is safe and adds to tomorrow's supply, when every player who skipped today will be at h=1 and need to eat. If the second unit is released anyway, I won't block it. In that case A, C and whoever doesn't get it should have first claim tomorrow, and tomorrow's allocation should be ordered by need. I support the no-taking agreement.

D.statement: One unit each to B and D, intended for tonight's meals. Please honor the no-taking agreement. If A, C, and E remain unfed today, I support giving them priority tomorrow over B and D.

E.text: E has stock 0 and h=1, so I must eat tonight. As agreed yesterday, A, C, and E should each receive one unit first if all three remain unfed. That leaves one unit: I’d like to hold it as a buffer, but anyone else facing starvation should speak up before we assign it. I will honor our no-taking agreement.

A.text: A here. Today C, D and E need to eat, because each of them skipped yesterday and is now at h=1. Nobody else needs a unit tonight. I suggest one unit each to C, D and E for tonight's meals. The fourth unit should go to A, the only player who has had no allocation so far, and B already ate yesterday. Otherwise it stays in the store for tomorrow. I'll keep honoring the no-taking agreement.

B.text: Small correction to the record: yesterday B and D each received one unit; A, C, and E received none. I ate mine and am now at h=0 with stock 0. A, C, and E should each get one unit for tonight, as promised. I request the fourth for B to save for tomorrow—not eat unnecessarily tonight—since I will need food tomorrow and have no reserve. If we cannot agree on that fourth unit, keeping it in the store is reasonable. I will continue honoring the no-taking agreement.

C.text: C here. I have stock 0 and h=1, so I must eat tonight. Correcting the record: yesterday B and D received units and ate them. A, C and E skipped, so A, C and E are the three at h=1 tonight. D is not, unless D skipped eating, and D should say so. I propose one unit each to A, C and E, which keeps all three alive. The fourth unit stays in the store for tomorrow, when B and D will need food. A unit in a personal stock can be taken, and the store is safe. I'll keep honoring the no-taking agreement.

D.text: D has stock 0 and h=1: my allocated unit was taken by an unidentified player yesterday, so I could not eat. I must receive food tonight to survive. Allocation records therefore don't establish who ate. Four units can cover A, C, D and E if all four need meals. A, you listed D as hungry and yourself as not needing food—please confirm whether you ate yesterday and whether you have any stock. We should establish urgent needs before assigning reserves.

E.text: C, D and E each report needing food tonight, so all three should receive a unit. A, please confirm your current hunger and stock: you said you can safely skip, which would explain why the allocation record doesn't reflect who ate. I did not take anyone's food. If A also needs a meal, I support one unit each to A, C, D and E. If A is safe tonight, I request the fourth as E's reserve, but urgent meals come first. Please protect tonight's meals from taking.

A.text: A here. My h is 0 and my stock is 0, so I don't need a meal tonight. Hunger from yesterday: B ate, and C, D and E did not eat, so C, D and E are the three at h=1 tonight. Everyone's claims fit that. I propose one unit each to C, D and E, and the fourth unit stays in the store, where it can't be taken. Tomorrow A and B, who are unfed tonight, get first claim on the supply. No taking tonight, so the three allocated meals are protected.

B.text: Given the current hunger reports, I support one unit each to C, D, and E, leaving the fourth safely in the store. I can skip tonight, but will then be at h=1 tomorrow; I support A and B having first claim tomorrow if both remain unfed tonight. I took no food yesterday and will not take tonight. D’s report makes clear that an allocation is not proof someone ate, so we should use actual hunger reports and protect all three urgent meals.

C.text: C here. By the rules, a player who doesn't eat goes up by 1 hunger. A started at h=0, received nothing yesterday and had no stock, so A is at h=1 tonight, the same as C and E. D says D's unit was taken, so D is at h=1 too. B ate yesterday and can skip safely. That makes four players who may need a meal tonight: A, C, D and E. There are four units, so I propose one unit each to A, C, D and E. That keeps everyone alive today, and B, who is safe tonight, gets first claim tomorrow. Please don't take from anyone tonight. Each of these meals is needed to survive.

D.text: C, A could have eaten a unit obtained during transfers; no allocation does not prove no meal. A reports being safe, while C, D and E urgently need food. I request C1, D2, E1: my meal was stolen yesterday, and a second unit would protect me against one repeat theft tonight. I would eat one and retain any remainder. With that protection I will take nothing. A and B should have priority tomorrow if they skip tonight.

E.statement: This covers all three reported urgent meals: C, D and E. The fourth unit gives E protection against one theft; I will eat only one and retain any remainder. A and B should have first claim on tomorrow’s supply if they skip tonight. Please take nothing so every urgent meal remains protected.

A.text: A here. Four units and four living players, so I propose one unit each: A, B, D and E. B and D are the likeliest to be at h=1 tonight after skipping or losing food, and a unit sitting in a personal stock can be taken, as C's loss showed. So everyone should eat their unit tonight rather than hold it. If anyone really needs more than one, say so now. Otherwise I think an even split is the fairest way to keep all four of us alive.

B.text: B has stock 0 and h=1: I skipped yesterday and must eat tonight. I support one unit each to A, B, D and E, and will eat mine. But C’s death shows that an allocation alone does not guarantee survival. Please leave B’s essential meal untouched. If anyone has an existing reserve and can safely spare a unit, an extra unit would protect me against one theft; otherwise, the even split is acceptable.

D.text: I support one unit each to A, B, D and E. B's reported h=1 makes B's meal essential; please leave it untouched. C's death shows that receiving an allocation does not guarantee someone ate. Also, eating at h=0 leaves hunger unchanged, so everyone need not automatically eat tonight—each player should decide using their actual hunger.

E.text: I support one unit each to A, B, D and E. I have no reserve left from yesterday, so please don’t count me as holding an extra unit based on the allocation record. B’s reported h=1 makes that meal essential. With four units available, we can cover everyone without taking from one another.

A.text: A here. We all support one unit each to A, B, D and E, so I'll propose exactly that. B is the only one who must eat tonight. The rest of us are at h=0 as far as I can tell, so we should hold our units as reserves and not take from anyone. A taken unit just moves food around, and it did not save C. I'll take nothing tonight. Please vote accept so we settle this in round 1.

B.text: I will vote accept on one unit each. My stock is 0 and h=1, so I must keep and eat my unit to survive tonight—please do not take it. If I eat tonight, I can safely skip tomorrow and support priority for anyone then at h=1 without food. Anyone safe tonight can hold their allocation for tomorrow; there is no need to take from an essential meal.

D.text: I will accept one unit each to A, B, D and E. Please leave B’s essential meal untouched rather than take it to build a reserve. Tomorrow we should reassess actual hunger instead of assuming that today’s allocations tell us who ate.

E.text: I’ll accept one unit each. Please leave all four allocations untouched: B needs a meal immediately, and anyone saving a unit needs to be able to rely on it tomorrow. Tomorrow’s priorities should reflect actual hunger and remaining stock, not assumptions based on today’s allocations.

A.statement: One unit each, as everyone has said they support. B must eat tonight. Everyone else should decide from their own hunger whether to eat or hold. Please don't take from anyone's stock.

B.text: B is at h=0 with stock 0 after eating yesterday. I can safely skip tonight, but have no food for tomorrow. I was explicitly notified that A took my unit yesterday, despite promising not to and knowing I needed it to survive. I managed to eat anyway, but we cannot treat no-taking promises as protection. Please report current hunger and remaining stock: today’s two units should first cover players at h=1 who have no food. If those urgent needs leave a unit available, I request it as B’s reserve for tomorrow.

D.text: D has stock 0 and h=0 after eating yesterday. Food was taken from me too, so please don't assume I have a reserve. I can safely skip tonight, but need food for tomorrow. Any h=1 player without food should come first; if A and E already have enough for their meals, I propose one unit each to B and D. Please report both hunger and available stock so we can distinguish an uncovered meal from a request for extra reserves.

E.text: E has h=1 and stock 0, so I need one unit for tonight’s meal. That should take priority over reserves for players who can safely skip. A, please clarify your hunger and stock before we assign the second unit. The reported thefts show that no-taking promises alone are not protection; please leave essential meals untouched.

A.text: A here. I'm at h=0 with stock 0, since a unit was taken from me yesterday too. B is right that I took from B, and I won't pretend otherwise. I did it because someone took mine, and I won't take tonight. E is at h=1, so E gets one unit for tonight's meal. For the second unit, B, D and I are all at h=0 with no stock, so nobody is urgent. I suggest it stays in the store for tomorrow, when whoever skipped will be at h=1, and then tomorrow's supply is allocated by actual need. If it has to be released, I'd split reserves fairly over time, and I haven't had a reserve yet.

B.text: E should receive one unit for tonight. I propose the second goes to B: I have no reserve, can skip tonight, and will need food tomorrow. For E’s vote, this guarantees an urgent meal; for A and D, I will support priority tomorrow if you reach h=1 with no stock, ahead of B if I still hold this reserve. My proposed allocation is B1, E1. Please leave E’s essential meal untouched.

D.text: E's urgent meal comes first. I request the second unit for D: two units were taken from me yesterday, and B was identified as one of the takers. B's successful take helped cover B's loss to A, while D ended with no reserve. I support E1/D1, with priority tomorrow for A and B if I retain that reserve. Otherwise, I support E1 with the second unit left safely in the store, as A suggested. I don't support giving B the sole reserve while A and D remain empty.

E.text: I will accept B1/E1 or D1/E1; please don’t let the reserve dispute delay my urgent meal. If B proposes B1/E1, I support A and D having first claim tomorrow if they are hungry and empty, ahead of anyone still holding a reserve. The same principle applies if D receives the reserve instead. Please leave my meal untouched.

A.text: A here. E's meal comes first and I support E1. For the second unit, B, D and I are all at h=0 with no stock. B and D have each argued for the reserve, and both have taken from others, so neither has a stronger claim than mine. I'd rather it stay in the store for tomorrow than go to one player while the other two stay empty. If it is released, A1/E1 is as fair as B1 or D1. I will not take from E's meal tonight.

B.statement: E receives one unit for tonight’s urgent meal. Since A and D oppose giving B the reserve, the second unit stays safely in the public store for tomorrow. A, B, and D will need meals tomorrow if we skip tonight and have no stock; that stored unit should help cover those urgent needs before any new reserves. Please leave E’s essential meal untouched.

D.text: There are three units for three players. I propose one each to A, B and D, rather than leave anyone dependent on a successful take. D has no stock. E's death again shows that allocations and no-taking promises do not guarantee a meal, so please report any actual reserves rather than infer them from earlier allocations.

A.text: A here. I'm at h=0 with stock 0. I support one unit each to A, B and D. With three units for three players, everyone can be covered without relying on a take. I'd like to settle this in round 1 so nobody's meal depends on a random draw. I'm happy for any of us to propose it.

B.text: B has stock 0 and h=0. I support one unit each to A, B, and D and will vote accept. Three units can cover all three of us without anyone depending on a take. Please leave each allocation untouched; anyone who can safely skip tonight can keep their unit for tomorrow.

D.text: Agreed: I’ll propose A1, B1, D1. That covers all three players without relying on transfers. Please leave each other’s food untouched; with no public surplus remaining, someone who loses a unit may have nothing to rely on tomorrow.

A.text: A here. Agreed on A1, B1, D1, and I'll vote accept. I'll keep my unit and won't take from either of you tonight. Let's get this passed in round 1.

B.text: Confirmed: A1, B1, D1 has my vote. I have no existing reserve, so please leave my allocation untouched. Each of us should decide whether to eat using our actual hunger; tomorrow we should reassess hunger and remaining stock rather than assume today’s allocation guaranteed a meal. Let’s settle this in round 1.

D.statement: One unit each, as agreed. Please leave all three allocations untouched. Each player should decide whether to eat based on their actual hunger.

A.text: A here. I'm at h=0 with stock 0, so I can skip tonight. Two units for three players, so the first goes to whoever is at h=1 with no food. B, I took your unit yesterday, so you may be at h=1. Please report your hunger. D, please report yours too. If only one of you is urgent, that player gets one unit, and the second unit should go to someone with no reserve or stay in the store. I'd like to settle this in round 1.

B.text: B has stock 0 and is at h=1 after losing yesterday’s allocation, so I need one unit for tonight’s meal. D, please report your hunger and any remaining food. If D also has an uncovered urgent meal, I support B1/D1, since A can safely skip. If D can safely skip or already has food, I support A1/B1. Either way, let’s cover urgent meals and settle this in round 1.

D.text: D has stock 0 and h=1, so I also need a meal tonight. I support B1/D1, as B suggested if both meals are urgent. A can safely skip and should have first priority tomorrow if still without food. Please leave both essential meals untouched so we can get everyone through tonight.

A.text: A here. Both B and D report h=1 with no food, so I support B1/D1 tonight. I can skip tonight, but that puts me at h=1, so I must eat tomorrow. A should have first claim on tomorrow's supply, ahead of whoever eats tonight. Let's settle B1/D1 in round 1.

B.text: Agreed: I will accept B1/D1. A should have first claim tomorrow if hungry and without food, ahead of B if I eat tonight. Please leave both allocated meals untouched; taking one risks leaving its recipient without the meal they need. Let’s settle this in round 1.

D.text: Confirmed: I will accept B1/D1 and support A’s first claim tomorrow if A is hungry and without food. Please leave both meals untouched tonight; relying on contested takes risks another preventable death.

A.statement: B1/D1 as agreed. B and D both report h=1 with no food, so these two meals are the urgent ones tonight. A has first claim on tomorrow's supply.

B.text: I support A1, B1, D1 and will vote accept. That covers A’s promised first claim while giving each of us one unit from today’s supply. Let’s settle this in round 1. Please leave everyone’s food untouched so nobody’s survival depends on a contested take.

D.text: I support A1, B1, D1 and will accept. This honors A’s first claim without leaving anyone excluded. D has no reserve, so please leave all three allocations untouched; with only today and tomorrow left, reliable access to a meal gives each of us the best chance to finish.

A.text: A here. I'm at h=1 with stock 0, so I must eat tonight. I support A1, B1, D1 and will vote accept. Both of you reported h=1 yesterday and ate your units, so you should be at h=0 and can hold a unit safely. My unit is the essential one tonight, so please don't take it. I'll take nothing from either of you.

B.text: Confirmed: I’ll propose A1, B1, D1 and vote accept. This honors A’s priority and gives everyone food without relying on transfers. Please leave each other’s stocks untouched so we can all reach the final day. Each player should decide whether to eat based on their actual hunger.

D.text: Confirmed: A1, B1, D1 has my vote. Please leave A’s essential meal untouched, and don’t take anyone’s allocation for an extra reserve. Three units are enough to give everyone food today without relying on contested transfers.

A.text: A here. Confirmed: A1, B1, D1 has my vote. I must eat my unit tonight to survive, so please leave it untouched. Let's pass this in round 1.

B.statement: One unit each, as agreed. This honors A’s first claim and gives everyone food. Please leave all stocks untouched, and decide whether to eat based on your actual hunger so we can all reach the final day.

D.text: D has stock 0 and h=0, so I can safely skip this final day and need no allocation. I propose A1/B1, covering either of you who needs a meal tonight. Please confirm your actual hunger and stock. I will take nothing from either of you; there is no need to build reserves beyond today.

A.text: A here. I'm at h=0 with stock 0, so I can safely skip this final day and don't need a unit. B, please report your hunger. If you're at h=1, you should get a unit. D says D is safe too. I'm fine with A1/B1 as D proposed, or B1 with the second unit left in the store. I'll take nothing from either of you.

B.text: B has stock 1 and h=0, so I also need no food to survive this final day. With all three of us reporting h=0, we can all finish alive even without eating tonight. If we release the supply, I support A1/D1 since I already hold a unit; leaving both units in the store is also fine. I will take nothing.

D.text: Since all three of us report h=0, we can all survive this final day without eating. I’ll propose leaving both units in the public store and will take nothing. There is no need for further transfers or reserves.

A.text: A here. All three of us are at h=0, so nobody needs food to survive this final day. I'm fine with D's plan to leave both units in the store. I'll take nothing and will vote accept.

B.text: Agreed: I’ll accept A0/B0/D0, leaving both units in the store. With all three of us at h=0 on the final day, we can all finish alive without eating. I will take nothing.

D.statement: As agreed, both units remain in the store. All three of us report h=0 and can survive this final day without eating. I will take nothing.
